$comment: THE CLAIMS LEDGER. This file is what makes fully-autonomous publishing safe.
Nothing goes live unless every factual assertion in it traces back to this file
or to machine-generated data in data/corpus-findings.json.
Rule: if you cannot point at a source, it does not go in 'verified'.
Anything in 'unverified' is BLOCKED from publication until it is substantiated.
fact-guard.mjs enforces this. Do not weaken it to get a post out the door.

verified.detail: 18 rules: ASI01-ASI10 (all ten OWASP Agentic categories), LLM01/02/05/06/07/10, and two EU AI Act Article 50 checks (EUAIA-52, EUAIA-50).
verified.source: Product source: src/rules/asi.ts and src/rules/llm.ts; asserted by test/scanner.test.js

verified.claim: Control-probe design: detects missing mitigations, not just dangerous keywords
verified.detail: Most rules fire only when a risk trigger is present AND no evidence of the standard mitigation exists in the corpus. This is materially different from grepping for eval().

verified.claim: Comments are stripped before mitigation evidence is matched
verified.detail: A `// TODO: add sandboxing` comment cannot satisfy a control probe and mark you as mitigated. Covered by a regression test.

verified.claim: Runs entirely offline, no telemetry, no network calls
verified.detail: One runtime dependency (picocolors). No HTTP client is imported anywhere in the scanner. Source code never leaves the machine.
verified.source: Product source: package.json dependencies; import inspection of src/

verified.detail: Terminal, Markdown (evidence document), JSON, and SARIF 2.1.0 which uploads to the GitHub code-scanning tab.
verified.source: Product source: src/report.ts; verified against the SARIF 2.1.0 schema

verified.claim: Detects patterns in TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, C# and Go
verified.detail: Polyglot fixtures assert that ASI01, ASI03 and ASI05 fire identically across .ts, .py, .cs and .go.

verified.claim: 30 adversarial red-team probes shipped as JSONL
verified.detail: Each probe is mapped to an OWASP ASI or LLM ID with a fail_signal, and is designed to be delivered through a real ingestion channel (retrieval, tool result, memory) rather than pasted into a chat box.
49 checks, with severity and an evidence column, covering the non-source factors static analysis cannot see, mapped to ASI01-ASI10.
verified.source: Product source: templates/manual-review-checklist.md (49 numbered rows, counted 2026-09-21)

verified.claim: Roughly 55% precision measured against five open-source agent frameworks (~3,100 source files)
verified.detail: HISTORICAL: measured on the August 2026 build, before the v1.5 false-positive fixes. It may only be cited as the figure for that build (e.g. 'the August build measured roughly 55% precision on five frameworks'), never as current precision. Precision for v1.5.2 is being re-measured across the 50-repository corpus; until that result is added here with a methodology file, say precision is being re-measured and give no current figure.

verified.claim: The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications was released by the OWASP GenAI Security Project's Agentic Security Initiative in December 2025
verified.detail: Announced 9 December 2025 after more than a year of research with 100+ contributors.

verified.claim: EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations took effect 2 August 2026
verified.detail: In force now. One narrow carve-out: generative systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 have until 2 December 2026 to implement Article 50(2) machine-readable marking. Everything else is live with no grace period.

verified.claim: The Digital Omnibus deferred Annex III high-risk obligations to December 2027, but did NOT defer Article 50
verified.detail: Use this to correct the widespread misreading that 'the August 2026 deadline moved.' It did not, for Article 50.

unverified.claim: 75-80% precision after tuning against 15 repositories / ~17,000 files
unverified.why: Nothing in the shipped product substantiates rounds two and three of this progression. The README states 5 repos / ~3,100 files / ~55%. Until a methodology file listing the 15 repositories and the measurement procedure ships with the product, this number is unpublishable and must be removed from the website.
unverified.unblockCondition: Ship docs/precision-methodology.md listing every repository scanned, the file counts, the triage procedure, and the raw counts. Then move this entry to verified and cite that file.

unverified.claim: Scans a 387-file Python repository in under a second
unverified.why: Measured in August on a repository that has since changed; no current repository in the corpus has 387 files. Speed claims now come only from durations measured in the corpus run (data/corpus-findings.json perRepo.durationMs).
unverified.unblockCondition: None. Use the measured figure the corpus brief supplies.
